speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to begin our investigation, how long have you been experiencing these coordination difficulties, and have you noticed any other neurological symptoms like weakness or speech changes?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reports recent onset of gait instability with a "drunk" appearance and clumsiness in the limbs, particularly on the right side. To narrow the differential between cerebellar degeneration, stroke, or structural lesions, have you experienced any episodes of vertigo, double vision, or difficulty swallowing since these symptoms began?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab use.
The combination of subacute ataxia, your history of Crohn's disease, and treatment with natalizumab (an immunosuppressant) strongly suggests an opportunistic infection of the CNS by JC virus. I request MRI images of the brain to confirm the diagnosis.
